PREMIERE316 STYLE-ONLY IMAGE REFERENCE CONTROL — V2
Asset ID: ward-elijah
Workflow profile: 4X3 (4:3)
Reference mode: ART DIRECTION ONLY — NO SUBJECT OR DESIGN TRANSFER.

The loaded images are non-content style plates. The asset prompt below is the sole authority for subject, identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, wardrobe design, prop design, environment geometry, creatures, crowd population, pose, action, camera composition, wounds, blood placement, text, and all story content.

ALLOWED TRANSFER ONLY: overall palette; contrast curve; key/fill/rim relationship; volumetric-light behavior; atmosphere density; material highlight and shadow response; lens/exposure language; practical texture fidelity; cinematic depth; restrained film grain.

FORBIDDEN TRANSFER: faces or facial geometry; body identity or proportions; hairstyles; costume silhouettes; wounds or blood maps; weapons or props; architecture or set geography; creature designs; crowd layout; pose; framing; four-panel layout; lettering; logos; or any recognizable object from a reference, unless the asset prompt itself explicitly requests that exact element.

Wardrobe guard: transfer only textile rendering, light response, practical aging, and filmic material quality. Do not introduce white burial linen, blood, sandals, or a body identity unless this row explicitly requires them.

Active plate roles: warm-gold lighting and highlight rolloff; smoky umber shadow palette and ember atmosphere; abstract filmic tonal/material response and restrained grain; explicitly requested production-sheet spacing/readability only.
When a reference conflicts with the row prompt, ignore the reference and obey the row prompt.

AUTHORITATIVE ASSET PROMPT
--------------------------
ANIMAL-SKIN PROPHETIC GARMENTS — PRODUCTION REFERENCE: COSTUME CONSTRUCTION, MATERIALS, FIT, DAMAGE, AND CONTINUITY.

Create a four-view cinematic character ingredients sheet showing the same person in frontal three-quarter portrait, full-body, side profile, and rear-head/costume view. Lock facial identity, age, ethnicity, hairline, complete crown and rear hair, costume construction, body proportions, hands, scars, wounds, and carried props across every panel. One face exists only on the front of the head. Photorealistic live-action production reference, physically coherent lighting, exact anatomy, clean hands, consistent scale and materials, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, and no written or graphical elements.

Four-view cinematic wardrobe ingredients sheet isolating the animal-skin prophetic garments of Elijah the Tishbite as worn in Hell's inner chamber at the moment of liberation—costume construction first, not a general character portrait. Present the same full costume system locked across four panels: (1) frontal three-quarter torso and upper garment detail showing mantle drape, collar opening, and leather girdle knot; (2) full-body front standing pose on a neutral dark stone plinth so hem length, bare lower legs, and sandal-free or rough hide foot wraps read clearly; (3) side profile full figure locking silhouette thickness of the mantle stack, belt line, and forward lean of prophetic stance; (4) rear-head and full rear costume view locking complete crown and rear hair falling over the mantle collar, rear hide seams, belt knot back, and how the cloak hangs from the shoulders with no face on the back of the head. One human face exists only on the front of the head; rear panel shows only hair, neck, and garment construction.

Costume identity—Elijah, not John the Baptist. This is a heavy layered prophetic mantle ensemble of authority and wilderness fire, visually distinct from John the Baptist's thinner single-layer rough camel-hair tunic. Elijah's kit is fuller, darker, more shaggy and mantle-like, built as a cloak-over-tunic system with a genuine leather girdle, recalling the hairy man with a leather belt of the prophets rather than the stripped ascetic prison rags of the Baptist.

Primary outer garment: a long shaggy mantle of coarse goat hair and dark camel hide, worn as a prophetic cloak wrapped and draped over both shoulders so it can be cast or gathered. Outer surface retains irregular tufts of coarse black-brown and iron-gray hair, sun-bleached in patches to dusty ochre and ash-tan. The hide is thick, stiff in places, supple and oil-dark at folds that have rubbed for years against desert rock and cave wall. Edges are uneven and hand-torn rather than tailored; lower hem hangs mid-calf to ankle with ragged points and hanging hair strands. Inner face of the mantle shows scraped hide underside—matte ochre, smoke-stained, with visible sinew stitch repairs and small bone or wooden toggles. Across the upper back and shoulders the mantle carries a scorched map of Carmel fire memory: faint char-black freckles, heat-cracked hide grain, and a permanent smoky bloom as if once stood too near sacred flame. Dust of Hell's chamber clings in the hair of the skins—pale ash powder in the deep pile, red-black grit at hem and cuff.

Under-layer: a shorter sleeveless or short-sleeved animal-hide tunic of lighter brown goatskin or sheepskin, worn close to the body beneath the mantle. The tunic reaches mid-thigh to just above the knee, leaving lean muscular arms and lower legs exposed. Seams are sinew-stitched with irregular primitive running stitches; underarms and side seams show age-stretched holes and careful re-lacing. Hair on the tunic is shorter and more worn-flat than the outer mantle, sun-baked to a warm dusty brown with greasy dark stains at the chest and waist where the leather girdle has sat for decades. No dyed cloth, no woven linen, no royal color—only hide, hair, leather, sinew, and ash.

Leather girdle (critical continuity prop of Elijah's wardrobe): a wide rawhide belt, two to three fingers high, dark oil-cured leather cinched hard about the loins over the tunic and under or through slits in the mantle. The leather is cracked, burnished black-brown at contact points, with a simple looped and knotted fastening rather than metal buckle. Frayed leather thongs hang from the knot. The girdle slightly compresses the hide folds and creates a clear waist break in the silhouette—this belt is the principal differentiator from John's looser unbelted or cord-tied skins.

Construction details to lock in every panel: overlapping hide panels at the chest; visible sinew whip-stitching; irregular hair direction following the animal's original grain; matted clumps where sweat and dust have felted the pile; small tears repaired with contrasting sinew; no metal hardware, no polished clasps, no jewelry, no woven trim. Hands and wrists may show if the figure is worn by a matching Elijah silhouette—weathered prophet hands, clean anatomy, no modern rings. Optional rough hide foot wraps or bare dusty feet only; no modern sandals with machine stitching.

Silhouette and fit on matching Elijah body type for continuity with char-elijah: mature desert prophet of late middle age to early elder years, lean but still powerful rather than prison-gaunt, shoulders slightly stooped from mantle weight, upright prophetic carriage. Mediterranean Levantine skin tone visible at face, neck, forearms, and calves where hide does not cover. Hair and beard of the wearer (when shown) long, coarse, salt-and-pepper to iron-dark, wind-wild, complete crown and rear coverage under and over the mantle collar—never a bald rear pate, never a second face on the back of the head. Eyes not the primary subject of this wardrobe sheet, but when the frontal panel includes the face, hold a banked furnace intensity in the gaze that reads as residual prophetic fire, not soft sadness.

Hell-chamber continuity state for this production beat: garments still carry the dust and cold of long captivity—ash film in hair of skins, faint chain-rub abrasion marks at wrists and across the upper arms where iron links once pressed the hide, slight blood-brown old stains at the hem from centuries of stone floor contact—not fresh battle gore. When divine gold light of the Harrowing begins to touch the chamber, the coarse hair of the mantle catches warm amber rim light while the recesses of the pile hold cold blue torch fill from remaining hellfire, so the costume reads in the liberation color arc without becoming clean or heavenly white.

Lighting for the ingredients sheet: physically coherent three-point production reference. Soft key from upper front-left at warm amber ~4500–5500K suggesting divine intrusion spill; cool fill from low side blue-torch ~2000K to preserve hell context in shadow folds of the hide; thin gold rim along mantle edge and hair silhouette. Shallow to moderate depth of field on detail close views so hide grain, individual coarse hairs, sinew stitches, and leather crackle are razor-sharp. Full-body panels keep the entire garment readable head to hem. Color grade: deep charcoal ground, ash and iron-gray hide, burnt umber and black-tipped goat hair, oil-black leather girdle, faint gold and blue crosslight—no saturated fantasy dyes, no modern fabric sheen.

Camera language: 50–85mm portrait and three-quarter detail panels; ~35–40mm full-body panels for honest proportions; 2.39:1 cinematic widescreen framing within each panel area; orthographic-feeling consistency of scale across the four views as a production ingredients board. Neutral dark stone or seamless shadowed void background so costume materials dominate—no readable architecture text, no banners, no modern stands with logos.

Hard differentiators from ward-john-the-baptist (must remain true): Elijah = heavy dual-layer mantle-plus-tunic, shaggy goat/camel hair pile with fire-scorch memory, wide rawhide leather girdle knotted at the loins, fuller drape to mid-calf/ankle, darker iron-gray and black-brown palette, prophet-of-fire authority. John = thinner single-layer rough animal-skin garment, more tattered and prison-worn, lighter dusty brown, gaunt body fit, no heavy mantle stack, stripped ascetic essentials. Never blend the two costumes.

Constraints: photoreal live-action biblical epic production wardrobe reference only; no illustration, no anime, no plastic CGI look; no modern objects, zippers, snaps, synthetic fleece, logos, brand marks, captions, watermarks, borders, UI, or any readable text or graphical labels on the image; one face only on the front of the head; exact garment construction locked across all four views; sacred reverent tone, not gore-porn or campy fantasy.
